title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the Sixth Batch of Guiding Cases
ruling_gist_en: Where a consumer purchases food that fails to meet food safety standards and demands that the seller or producer pay compensation of ten times the purchase price in accordance with the Food Safety Law, or pay compensation according to other statutory compensation standards, the people's court shall support such a claim, regardless of whether the consumer knew at the time of purchase that the food did not meet the safety standards.
keywords_en: Civil Law; Sales Contract; Food Safety; Tenfold Compensation
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Issuing the Sixth Batch of Guiding Cases

Fa [2014] No. 18

To the High People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

Upon discussion and decision by the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court, the four cases including Sun Yinshan v. Nanjing Auchan Supermarket Co., Ltd., Jiangning Branch — dispute over sales contract (Guiding Cases No. 23-26) are hereby issued as the sixth batch of guiding cases for reference in adjudicating similar cases.

January 26, 2014

Guiding Case No. 23

Sun Yinshan v. Nanjing Auchan Supermarket Co., Ltd., Jiangning Branch — dispute over sales contract

(Deliberated and adopted by the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court, issued on January 26, 2014)

Keywords: civil; sales contract; food safety; ten-fold compensation

Ruling Gist

Where a consumer purchases food that does not meet food safety standards and demands that the seller or producer pay ten times the purchase price as compensation in accordance with the Food Safety Law or pay compensation under other statutory compensation standards, the people's court shall support such claim regardless of whether the consumer knew at the time of purchase that the food did not meet the safety standards.

Related Legal Provisions

Article 96, Paragraph 2 of the Food Safety Law of the People's Republic of China

Basic Facts

On May 1, 2012, the plaintiff, Sun Yinshan, purchased 15 packages of "Yutu Brand" sausages from the defendant, Nanjing Auchan Supermarket Co., Ltd., Jiangning Branch (hereinafter "Auchan Supermarket Jiangning Branch"), of which 14 packages with a value of RMB 558.6 had exceeded their shelf life. After Sun Yinshan checked out at the cashier, he immediately went to the service counter to claim compensation. After negotiations failed, he filed a lawsuit with the court, demanding that Auchan Supermarket Jiangning Branch pay him ten times the sale price of the 14 packages of sausages, i.e., RMB 5,586.

Judgment

The Jiangning District People's Court of Nanjing, Jiangsu Province, rendered a civil judgment (2012) Jiangning Kaimin Chuzi No. 646 on September 10, 2012: The defendant, Auchan Supermarket Jiangning Branch, shall compensate the plaintiff, Sun Yinshan, RMB 5,586 within 10 days from the date the judgment takes legal effect. After the judgment was pronounced, neither party appealed, and the judgment has taken legal effect.

Reasoning

The effective judgment of the court held:

Concerning whether the plaintiff, Sun Yinshan, qualifies as a consumer: Article 2 of the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Consumer Rights and Interests provides: "Consumers who purchase, use, or receive services for the purpose of daily consumption shall have their rights and interests protected under this Law; where this Law does not provide for such protection, it shall be provided under other relevant laws and regulations." The term "consumer" is relative to the concepts of seller and producer. As long as the purchase, use, or receipt of services in a market transaction is for personal or household living needs, rather than for production or business activities or occupational needs, the person shall be deemed a consumer purchasing or using commodities or receiving services "for the purpose of daily consumption" and falls within the scope of adjustment of the Law on the Protection of Consumer Rights and Interests. In this case, both the plaintiff and defendant did not dispute the fact that Sun Yinshan purchased sausages from Auchan Supermarket Jiangning Branch. Based on this, it can be established that Sun Yinshan engaged in the act of purchasing commodities, and Sun Yinshan did not resell the purchased sausages for business operations. Auchan Supermarket Jiangning Branch also failed to provide evidence to prove that the purchase of commodities was for production or business operations. Sun Yinshan's claim for compensation due to the purchase of food that had exceeded its shelf life constitutes the exercise of a statutory right. Therefore, the defense of Auchan Supermarket Jiangning Branch that Sun Yinshan was not a consumer because he "purchased fake goods to claim compensation" cannot be sustained.

Concerning whether the defendant, Auchan Supermarket Jiangning Branch, sold food that it knew did not meet food safety standards: Article 3 of the Food Safety Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter "Food Safety Law") provides: "Food production and business operators shall engage in production and business activities in accordance with laws, regulations, and food safety standards, be responsible to society and the public, ensure food safety, accept social supervision, and bear social responsibility." Article 28(8) of the same Law provides that food that has exceeded its shelf life is prohibited from being produced and marketed. Food sellers bear a statutory duty to ensure food safety and shall promptly remove food that does not meet safety standards on their own. As a food seller, Auchan Supermarket Jiangning Branch was required to store food in accordance with the requirements of ensuring food safety, promptly inspect food for sale, and clear out food that has exceeded its shelf life. However, Auchan Supermarket Jiangning Branch still displayed and sold "Yutu Brand" sausages on the shelves that had exceeded their shelf life, thereby failing to perform its statutory duty. This can be deemed as selling food that it knew did not meet food safety standards.

Concerning the liability of the defendant, Auchan Supermarket Jiangning Branch: Article 96, Paragraph 1 of the Food Safety Law provides: "Whoever violates the provisions of this Law and causes personal, property, or other damage shall bear liability for compensation in accordance with the law." Paragraph 2 provides: "Where food that does not meet food safety standards is produced or food that is knowingly sold does not meet food safety standards, in addition to claiming damages, the consumer may also demand from the producer or seller the payment of ten times the purchase price as compensation." When a seller knowingly sells food that does not meet safety standards, the consumer may claim both damages and ten times the purchase price as compensation, or may claim only ten times the purchase price as compensation. In this case, the plaintiff, Sun Yinshan, only demanded that Auchan Supermarket Jiangning Branch pay ten times the sale price as compensation. This is an act of the party disposing of its own rights and should be supported. As to the defendant's contention that the plaintiff knew the food was expired at the time of purchase and intended to exploit the defendant's error for profit, and therefore should not be entitled to ten times compensation, because the aforementioned legal provision grants consumers the right to obtain ten times the purchase price as compensation, and the benefits obtained from such compensation are legally protected interests, and the law does not impose any restrictive provisions on the subjective shopping motives of consumers, the court does not support this contention.

Guiding Case No. 24

Rong Baoying v. Wang Yang and Yongcheng Property Insurance Co., Ltd., Jiangyin Branch — dispute over liability for motor vehicle traffic accident

(Deliberated and adopted by the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court, issued on January 26, 2014)

Keywords: civil; traffic accident; fault liability

Ruling Gist

Where the victim of a traffic accident is not at fault, the influence of the victim's physical condition on the consequences of the damage does not constitute a statutory circumstance that may reduce the liability of the tortfeasor.

Related Legal Provisions

Article 26 of the Tort Liability Law of the People's Republic of China

Article 76, Paragraph 1, Item (2) of the Road Traffic Safety Law of the People's Republic of China

Basic Facts

The plaintiff, Rong Baoying, alleged: The defendant, Wang Yang, while driving a car, scraped against her, causing her injury. The traffic accident was determined by the Binhu Brigade of the Traffic Patrol Police Detachment of Wuxi Public Security Bureau, Jiangsu Province (hereinafter "Binhu Traffic Police Brigade"), that Wang Yang bore full responsibility for the accident, and Rong Baoying was not at fault. The plaintiff requested the two defendants below to pay medical expenses of RMB 30,006, hospitalization meal subsidies of RMB 414, nutrition expenses of RMB 1,620, disability compensation of RMB 27,658.05, nursing expenses of RMB 6,000, transportation expenses of RMB 800, and moral damages of RMB 10,500, and to bear the litigation costs and appraisal fees.

The defendant, Yongcheng Property Insurance Co., Ltd., Jiangyin Branch (hereinafter "Yongcheng Insurance Company"), argued: It had no objection to the accident process and liability determination, and it was willing to pay compensation within the limits of compulsory traffic accident liability insurance; it had no objection to the medical expenses of RMB 30,006 and hospitalization meal subsidies of RMB 414; since the conclusion of the expert opinion stated that "the degree of injury participation was assessed at 75%, and the factor of the individual's physical constitution accounted for 25%," the disability compensation should be multiplied by a factor of 0.75 for the degree of injury participation, and RMB 20,743.54 was recognized; for nutrition expenses, RMB 1,350 was recognized; for nursing expenses, RMB 3,300 was recognized; for transportation expenses, RMB 400 was recognized; and the appraisal fees were not to be borne.

The defendant, Wang Yang, argued: He had no objection to the accident process and liability determination; the plaintiff's losses should be compensated first by Yongcheng Insurance Company within the limits of compulsory traffic accident liability insurance; the appraisal fees should be determined by the court according to law; he agreed with the insurance company's opinions on the remaining expenses; and he had already paid the plaintiff RMB 20,000 in compensation.

The court found through trial: At approximately 2:45 p.m. on February 10, 2012, Wang Yang was driving a car with license plate Su MT1888 heading north on Lihu Avenue in Binhu District, Wuxi City, Jiangsu Province. When he reached the pedestrian crosswalk at the intersection of Lihu Avenue and Datong Road, he scraped against the pedestrian Rong Baoying, causing her injury. On February 11, the Binhu Traffic Police Brigade issued a "Road Traffic Accident Determination," finding that Wang Yang bore full responsibility for the accident and Rong Baoying was not at fault. On the day of the accident, Rong Baoying was immediately taken to the hospital for treatment, incurring medical expenses of RMB 30,006, of which Wang Yang advanced RMB 20,000. During Rong Baoying's treatment and recovery period, she hired a domestic helper at a monthly fee of RMB 2,200. The car with license plate Su MT1888 was insured with Yongcheng Insurance Company under compulsory motor vehicle traffic accident liability insurance, with the insurance period from 0:00 on August 17, 2011, to 24:00 on August 16, 2012. The plaintiff and defendants jointly confirmed that Rong Baoying's medical expenses were RMB 30,006, hospitalization meal subsidies were RMB 414, and moral damages were RMB 10,500.

At Rong Baoying's request, the Judicial Expertise Institute of Wuxi Integrated Traditional Chinese and Western Medicine Hospital conducted an appraisal, concluding: 1. The disability grade for Rong Baoying's left distal radius fracture was assessed as Grade 10; the disability grade for her left lower limb injury was assessed as Grade 9. The degree of injury participation was assessed at 75%, with the factor of the individual's physical constitution accounting for 25%. 2. Rong Baoying's period of lost work was assessed as 150 days, the nursing period as 60 days, and the nutrition period as 90 days. Based on this, the court of first instance determined that disability compensation of RMB 27,658.05 should be reduced by 25% to RMB 20,743.54.

Judgment

The Binhu District People's Court of Wuxi, Jiangsu Province, rendered a judgment (2012) Xibin Min Chuzi No. 1138 on February 8, 2013: 1. The defendant, Yongcheng Insurance Company, shall, within 10 days after this judgment takes effect, compensate Rong Baoying a total of RMB 45,343.54 for medical expenses, hospitalization meal subsidies, nutrition expenses, disability compensation, nursing expenses, transportation expenses, and moral damages. 2. The defendant, Wang Yang, shall, within 10 days after this judgment takes effect, compensate Rong Baoying a total of RMB 4,040 for medical expenses, hospitalization meal subsidies, nutrition expenses, and appraisal fees. 3. The other claims of the plaintiff, Rong Baoying, are dismissed. After the judgment was pronounced, Rong Baoying appealed to the Wuxi Intermediate People's Court, Jiangsu Province. Upon trial, the Wuxi Intermediate People's Court rendered a civil judgment (2013) Ximin Zhongzi No. 497 on June 21, 2013, holding that the original trial erred in the application of law: 1. The civil judgment (2012) Xibin Min Chuzi No. 1138 of the Binhu District People's Court of Wuxi is vacated; 2. The defendant, Yongcheng Insurance Company, shall, within 10 days after this judgment takes effect, compensate Rong Baoying RMB 52,258.05; 3. The defendant, Wang Yang, shall, within 10 days after this judgment takes effect, compensate Rong Baoying RMB 4,040; 4. The other claims of the plaintiff, Rong Baoying, are dismissed.

Reasoning

The effective judgment of the court held: Article 26 of the Tort Liability Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "If the injured party is also at fault for the occurrence of the damage, the liability of the tortfeasor may be reduced." Article 76, Paragraph 1, Item (2) of the Road Traffic Safety Law of the People's Republic of China provides that where a motor vehicle is involved in a traffic accident with a non-motor vehicle driver or a pedestrian, if the non-motor vehicle driver or pedestrian is not at fault, the motor vehicle party shall bear the liability for compensation; if there is evidence that the non-motor vehicle driver or pedestrian is at fault, the liability of the motor vehicle party shall be appropriately reduced according to the degree of fault. Therefore, in calculating whether to reduce disability compensation in a traffic accident, it is necessary to analyze whether the victim was at fault for the occurrence or enlargement of the loss. In this case, although the plaintiff, Rong Baoying's individual physical condition had some influence on the occurrence of the consequences of the damage, this does not constitute fault as defined in the Tort Liability Law and other laws. Rong Baoying should not bear corresponding responsibility solely because her physical condition had some influence on the disability caused by the traffic accident. The original trial judgment's reduction in calculating disability compensation on the ground that the disability grade appraisal concluded that the "degree of injury participation of Rong Baoying's individual physical condition was assessed at 75%" constituted an error in the application of law and should be corrected.

Viewed from the perspective of causation between the victim's injury and the consequences of the damage in a traffic accident, the cause of this traffic accident was that the tortfeasor, Wang Yang, while driving a motor vehicle crossing a pedestrian crosswalk, failed to exercise due care and scraped against the pedestrian, Rong Baoying. The consequences of the damage in this traffic accident were caused by Rong Baoying being hit by the motor vehicle, falling, and fracturing her bones. The accident liability determination found Rong Baoying not liable for this accident, and she had no fault in either the occurrence of the accident or the consequences of the damage. Although Rong Baoying was of advanced age, her elderly osteoporosis was merely an objective factor contributing to the consequences of the accident and did not have a legal causal relationship. Therefore, the victim, Rong Baoying, was not at fault for the occurrence or enlargement of the damage, and there is no statutory circumstance for reducing or exempting the tortfeasor's liability for compensation. At the same time, motor vehicles shall abide by the general traffic rules and social ethics of civilized driving and giving way to pedestrians. The accident in this case occurred on a pedestrian crosswalk. Rong Baoying, who was walking normally, could not have foreseen that she would be hit by a motor vehicle, while Wang Yang, driving a motor vehicle, failed to slow down and avoid pedestrians as required by law when crossing a pedestrian crosswalk, thereby causing the accident. Therefore, the motor vehicle party shall bear full liability for compensation arising from the accident in accordance with the law.

According to the relevant provisions of the Road Traffic Safety Law of the People's Republic of China, where a motor vehicle traffic accident causes personal injury or property damage, the insurance company shall pay compensation within the limits of the compulsory third-party liability insurance for motor vehicles. The legislation on compulsory traffic accident liability insurance does not provide that when determining liability under such insurance, the influence of the victim's physical condition on the consequences of the damage shall be taken into account for a corresponding reduction. The grounds for exemption of the insurance company are limited to situations where the victim intentionally causes the traffic accident. Even if the insured motor vehicle is not at fault, the insurance company shall still pay compensation within the limit of no-fault liability under the compulsory insurance. Therefore, losses of the victim that conform to the compensation items and standards prescribed by law are within the scope of compensation under the compulsory insurance. It is not legally justified to determine liability for damages or liability under compulsory insurance by reference to the "degree of injury participation."

Guiding Case No. 25

Huatai Property Insurance Co., Ltd., Beijing Branch v. Li Zhigui and Tianan Property Insurance Co., Ltd., Hebei Branch, Zhangjiakou Sub-Branch — dispute over insurer's subrogation right

(Deliberated and adopted by the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court, issued on January 26, 2014)

Keywords: civil litigation; insurer's subrogation right; jurisdiction

Ruling Gist

Where a third party's damage to the subject matter insured causes an insured event, and after paying insurance compensation to the insured, the insurer files a lawsuit to exercise the insured's right to claim compensation against the third party by way of subrogation, the court with jurisdiction shall be determined based on the legal relationship between the insured, on whose behalf the insurer exercises subrogation, and the third party, not on the insurance contract legal relationship. Where the third party infringes upon the lawful rights and interests of the insured, the court of the place where the tort was committed or the place where the defendant has its domicile shall have jurisdiction.

Related Legal Provisions

Article 28 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China

Article 60, Paragraph 1 of the Insurance Law of the People's Republic of China

Basic Facts

On June 1, 2011, Huatai Property Insurance Co., Ltd., Beijing Branch (hereinafter "Huatai Insurance Company") entered into a motor vehicle insurance contract with Beijing Yada Jindu Catering Management Co., Ltd. (hereinafter "Yada Jindu Catering Company"). The insured vehicle's license plate was Jing A82368, with the insurance period from 0:00 on June 5, 2011, to 24:00 on June 4, 2012. On November 18, 2011, Chen Moumou was driving the insured vehicle on the airport expressway in Chaoyang District, Beijing, when it collided with a vehicle with license plate Ji GA9120 driven by Li Zhigui, causing damage to the insured vehicle. The traffic management department determined that Li Zhigui bore full responsibility for the accident. After the accident, Huatai Insurance Company paid insurance compensation of RMB 83,878 to the insured, Yada Jindu Catering Company, in accordance with the insurance contract, and lawfully obtained the right of subrogation. Since the vehicle at fault was insured with Tianan Property Insurance Co., Ltd., Hebei Branch, Zhangjiakou Sub-Branch (hereinafter "Tianan Insurance Company") under compulsory motor vehicle traffic accident liability insurance, Huatai Insurance Company filed a lawsuit in November 2012 with the Dongcheng District People's Court of Beijing, requesting that the defendant, Li Zhigui (the at-fault driver), and Tianan Insurance Company be ordered to pay RMB 83,878 and bear the litigation costs.

The domicile of the defendant, Li Zhigui, was Shacheng Town, Huailai County, Zhangjiakou, Hebei Province. The domicile of the defendant, Tianan Insurance Company, was No. 108, Yanjing Road East, Shacheng Town, Huailai County, Zhangjiakou. The place where the insured event occurred was the airport expressway in Chaoyang District, Beijing. The address recorded on the driving license of the insured vehicle as the owner's address was No. 8, Xinzhongxi Street, Gongti North Road, Dongcheng District, Beijing.

Judgment

The Dongcheng District People's Court of Beijing rendered a civil ruling (2012) Dongmin Chuzi No. 13663 on December 17, 2012: The lawsuit filed by Huatai Insurance Company is not accepted. After the ruling was pronounced, the parties did not appeal, and the ruling has taken legal effect.

Reasoning

The effective judgment of the court held: According to Article 60 of the Insurance Law of the People's Republic of China, the insurer's right of subrogation refers to the right enjoyed by the insurer by law to exercise, in the place of the insured, the right to claim compensation against the third party who is liable for damage to the subject matter insured. The insurer's right of subrogation originates from direct statutory provisions and is a statutory right of the insurer, not a contractual right arising from the insurance contract. Where a third party's damage to the subject matter insured causes an insured event, and after paying insurance compensation to the insured, the insurer files a lawsuit to exercise the insured's right to claim compensation against the third party by way of subrogation, the court with jurisdiction shall be determined based on the legal relationship between the insured, on whose behalf the insurer exercises subrogation, and the third party. Where the third party infringes upon the lawful rights and interests of the insured, a lawsuit arising from a tort, pursuant to Article 28 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, shall be under the jurisdiction of the people's court of the place where the tort was committed or the place where the defendant has its domicile, and the provisions on jurisdiction over disputes over property insurance contracts shall not apply, nor shall the location of the subject matter insured be used as the basis for jurisdiction. In this case, the third party committed a road traffic tort, causing an insured event. The insured has a right to claim tort damages against the third party. Where the insurer exercises the right of subrogation and sues the third party, the court of the place where the tort was committed or the place where the defendant has its domicile shall have jurisdiction. Now, the domiciles of both defendants and the place of the tort are not within Dongcheng District, Beijing. Therefore, the Dongcheng District People's Court of Beijing has no jurisdiction over this lawsuit and should rule that the lawsuit is not accepted.

Guiding Case No. 26

Li Jianxiong v. Department of Transport of Guangdong Province — dispute over government information disclosure

(Deliberated and adopted by the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court, issued on January 26, 2014)

Keywords: administrative; government information disclosure; online application; overdue reply

Ruling Gist

If a citizen, legal person, or other organization submits an application for government information disclosure to an administrative organ through a government public network system, and the system does not provide an exceptional note to the contrary, the date on which the system confirms the successful submission of the application shall be deemed the date on which the administrative organ received the application. The internal processing procedures of the administrative organ with respect to the application shall not constitute a justification for the administrative organ's delay in handling, and a response made after the expiration of the statutory period shall be confirmed as unlawful.

Relevant Laws

Article 24 of the Regulations of the People's Republic of China on Open Government Information

Basic Facts

Plaintiff Li Jianxiong alleged: On June 1, 2011, he submitted an application for government information disclosure to the defendant, the Department of Transportation of Guangdong Province, through the Guangdong Provincial People's Government Public Network System. Pursuant to Article 24(2) of the Regulations of the People's Republic of China on Open Government Information (hereinafter referred to as the "Regulations on Open Government Information"), the defendant should have responded to the plaintiff by June 23 of that month. However, the defendant failed to respond within the statutory period or provide the requested government information. Therefore, the plaintiff requested that the court confirm that the defendant's failure to respond within the statutory period was unlawful.

The defendant, the Department of Transportation of Guangdong Province, argued: The plaintiff submitted his application for government information disclosure through the Guangdong Provincial People's Government Public Network System, i.e., the provincial government's external network (hereinafter referred to as the "provincial external network"), rather than the defendant's internal local area network (hereinafter referred to as the "departmental internal network"). Pursuant to regulations, the defendant had set up the backend processing for the Guangdong Provincial People's Government's "Online Application System for Government Information Disclosure" on the departmental internal network. Because the departmental internal network is physically isolated from the Internet and the provincial external network, data from the Internet and the provincial external network could not directly enter the departmental internal network for processing; it could only be transferred via a gateway through a data "ferry" into the departmental internal network for processing. Accordingly, the defendant's staff failed to immediately discover the application submitted by the plaintiff in the Guangdong Provincial People's Government Public Network System, resulting in the defendant's failure to accept the application in a timely manner. Pursuant to Article 24 of the Regulations on Open Government Information and the Notice of the General Office of the State Council on Preparatory Work for Implementing the Regulations of the People's Republic of China on Open Government Information, acceptance of an application in government information disclosure is based not on the date the applicant submits the application, but on the date the administrative organ receives the application. The plaintiff claimed to have submitted an application to the defendant on June 1, 2011, but the defendant did not receive it. The defendant formally received and confirmed acceptance of the application on July 28, and issued a "Receipt of Acceptance" to the plaintiff as required. On August 4, the defendant served the plaintiff on site with the "Reply on Government Information Disclosure" and the "Response to Government Information Disclosure," which was only 5 working days after the date of acceptance and did not exceed the statutory response period. Since the failure to promptly discover and accept the application submitted by the plaintiff through the government public network system should be attributed to force majeure or objective reasons, this period should not be counted within the response period. Accordingly, the defendant requested that the court reject the plaintiff's claim.

The court found through trial: On June 1, 2011, the plaintiff, Li Jianxiong, submitted an application for government information disclosure to the defendant, the Department of Transportation of Guangdong Province, through the Guangdong Provincial People's Government Public Network System, requesting access to government information such as the passenger mileage from Guangzhou Guangyuan Coach Station to Fogang. The government public network system generated Application No. 11060100011 to confirm the submission and notified the plaintiff via SMS that the submission of the application for government information disclosure was successful. On July 28, the defendant made a record of acceptance confirming the above facts, and on August 4, it served the plaintiff with the "Reply on Government Information Disclosure" and the "Response to Government Information Disclosure." During the trial, the defendant confirmed that the plaintiff sought the said information based on his needs in daily life and production, and the plaintiff confirmed that he received the "Reply on Government Information Disclosure" and the "Response to Government Information Disclosure" from the defendant on August 4.

Judgment

The Yuexiu District People's Court of Guangzhou rendered an administrative judgment on August 24, 2011 [(2011) Yuefa Xingchuzi No. 252]: confirming that the defendant, the Department of Transportation of Guangdong Province, failed to respond within the period prescribed by Article 24 of the Regulations on Open Government Information to the plaintiff Li Jianxiong's application of June 1, 2011, for disclosure of government information concerning the passenger mileage from Guangzhou Guangyuan Coach Station to Fogang, and that such failure was unlawful.

Reasoning

The effective judgment of the court held: Article 24 of the Regulations on Open Government Information provides: "If an administrative organ can respond on the spot upon receiving an application for government information disclosure, it shall do so. If the administrative organ cannot respond on the spot, it shall respond within 15 working days from the date of receipt of the application; if an extension of the response period is necessary, it shall be approved by the person in charge of the government information disclosure working body, and the applicant shall be informed; the maximum extension period shall not exceed 15 working days." In this case, the plaintiff submitted an application for government information disclosure to the defendant through the Guangdong Provincial People's Government Public Network System on June 1, 2011, requesting disclosure of the passenger mileage from Guangzhou Guangyuan Coach Station to Fogang. The government public network system generated a corresponding electronic application number and sent a text message to the plaintiff's mobile phone confirming the successful submission. The defendant confirmed receipt of the said application and acknowledged that the plaintiff sought the information based on his needs in daily life and production; nevertheless, the defendant did not issue the "Reply on Government Information Disclosure" and the "Response to Government Information Disclosure" to the plaintiff until August 4, 2011, thereby exceeding the statutory response period prescribed above. Given the integrated and authoritative nature that the Guangdong Provincial People's Government "Online Application System for Government Information Disclosure" should possess as a platform for submitting applications for government information disclosure, unless an exceptional note is made to the contrary, an application successfully submitted through that platform shall be deemed to have been received by the relevant administrative organ as an application submitted via the Internet. As for the transfer of the application between the external network and the internal network, or between higher and lower administrative organs, that pertains to internal administrative management affairs and cannot constitute a justification for the administrative organ's delay in handling. The defendant's argument that the plaintiff submitted the application through the government public network system and that, due to the physical isolation of its departmental internal network from the Internet and the provincial external network, it could not promptly discover the plaintiff's application, and that the date of receipt should be July 28, 2011, when it discovered the application, thus not exceeding the response period, was untenable. Therefore, where the plaintiff submits an application for government information disclosure through the government public network system, the date on which the system confirms the successful submission shall be deemed the date on which the defendant received the application. Accordingly, the defendant's overdue response must be confirmed as unlawful.
